item.title: 'Mar gaya, mar gaya tera bhai': How row over metro seat turned deadly in Delhi
item.description: A tragic altercation on a Delhi Metro train claimed the life of Pawan Sharma, the sole breadwinner of his family, on October 8. His death has left his wife and two children in deep sorrow. Authorities have taken action, arresting the individuals involved in the confrontation over reserved seating, and the case is currently under investigation for culpable homicide.
item.dc:creator: ABHAY

item.title: 6.1-magnitude earthquake strikes off Panama
item.description: On Monday evening, Panama was shaken by a 6.1 magnitude earthquake, closely following a more powerful 7.7 quake that had already wreaked havoc. Homes, roads, and public infrastructure suffered severe damage, especially in Coclé province and Panama City. In response, the government declared a state of emergency to manage relief efforts, while the US Embassy alerted nations across Central and South America about possible aftershocks and tsunami risks.

item.title: 2036 Olympic hosts: Ahmedabad vs South Korea, Qatar, Munich, and 3 more
item.description: As Ahmedabad builds its case to host the 2036 Olympics, it faces competition from cities and countries with different advantages. From Munich’s existing venues and Qatar’s event-ready infrastructure to South Korea’s regional model, South Africa’s continental ambition, Istanbul’s Olympic experience and Hungary’s low-construction approach, each offers challenge, and lessons, for India.

item.title: Washington farmer challenges $618,000 irrigation penalties in state Supreme Court
item.description: Ron Fodé, a dedicated farmer from Washington State, is fighting against hefty penalties threatening his agricultural livelihood due to irrigation practices. The conflict arose in 2017 over water rights for his crops, leading to the Department of Ecology rejecting his irrigation assistance applications. This has resulted in penalties totaling $618,000.

item.title: Pope withdraws from Afghan league draft amid concerns over treatment of women
item.description: England batter Ollie Pope has withdrawn from the Afghanistan Premier League draft amid concerns over the Taliban’s treatment of women and girls. England cricket director Rob Key said participation was a personal moral decision, despite the ECB’s refusal to arrange bilateral series with Afghanistan. Former England batter Dawid Malan remains in the draft, highlighting the conflict between ethical concerns and players’ livelihoods.

item.title: £10 Lowry painting kept 99 years sells for £805,200 at auction
item.description: An LS Lowry painting sold for over £805,000 at an auction after nearly a century in a family collection. Arthur Wallace, a British newspaper editor, purchased it for just £10 back in 1926. The painting, known as Going to the Mill, was created in 1925 and reflects Lowry's artistic focus on industrial life. The artwork highlights the transformation of its value from a lesser-known artist to a celebrated figure.

item.title: Roloff's $185K farm now at center of family feud 36 years later
item.description: Matt and Amy Roloff bought their 16-acre Oregon farm for $185,000 in 1990, long before Little People, Big World brought the family fame. Now, 36 years later, their son Jacob and his wife, Isabel, face the possibility of leaving the property as Matt considers selling more of the land, leaving them devastated about their future.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Before radar, Britain tried to hear enemy bombers coming using giant concrete ‘ears’
item.description: Britain’s Denge Sound Mirrors, three concrete structures on the Kent coast built between 1928 and 1930, were designed to catch the drone of approaching bombers and give defenders a few extra minutes of warning. Led by physicist Dr William Sansome Tucker, the project followed heavy World War 1 air raids on coastal towns. Faster aircraft, background noise and the arrival of radar made the mirrors obsolete by 1939.

item.title: 7 kitchen ingredients that keep cockroaches away
item.description: A tidy and hygienic kitchen is vital for preventing cockroach invasions. Using everyday ingredients like bay leaves and garlic powder can act as natural repellents. Cleaning with soapy water on a consistent basis helps eliminate food scraps that attract these pests. Additionally, storing food in sealed containers further reduces their interest. In cases of heavy infestations, seeking help from pest control experts could provide a more effective long-term fix.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Brain cancer diagnosis: Man blamed headaches on stress before scan revealed tumour
item.description: At first, Kash Raju dismissed his worsening health as the result of stress and a busy family routine. However, persistent headaches and dizziness led him to seek medical assistance, where a CT scan disclosed a diagnosis of grade 4 astrocytoma, an aggressive brain cancer. He promptly had emergency surgery and began NHS treatment, with a prognosis suggesting he may have only 12 to 18 months left.

item.title: Naomi Osaka reveals how daughter Shai changed her life beyond tennis
item.description: Naomi Osaka has opened up about her mental health struggles, crediting motherhood and her daughter, Shai, with helping her find happiness beyond tennis. The four-time Grand Slam champion revealed how her perspective has changed since her 2021 French Open withdrawal, when she disclosed her battle with depression and anxiety. After defeating Maria Timofeeva at the China Open, Osaka reflected on personal growth, gratitude and learning to balance her professional career with life outside tennis.

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reveals he translated English for Messi at award ceremonies
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has opened up about his 15-year rivalry with Lionel Messi, revealing how he helped the Argentine understand English during award ceremonies. The Al-Nassr star described their relationship as respectful and their competition as healthy, comparing it to Ayrton Senna and Alain Prost. However, Ronaldo remains firm in his belief that his remarkable goalscoring record makes him football’s greatest ever.

item.title: He gave land given for road, sold TDRs for Rs 6.02 crore; ITAT taxes capital gains
item.description: The landowner chose to sell the TDRs he had received for surrendering 2,839 square metres of land. He sold them to a builder for Rs 6 crore but did not pay income tax on the proceeds. His understanding was that the amount received from the sale was a capital receipt and was therefore not taxable.

item.title: Kerala crash: Old video shows accused teen’s Mini Cooper speeding at 220kmph
item.description: Suhail Sajeev, a 19-year-old, was arrested after a crash in Nedumbassery that killed three people. The victims were returning home on a scooter when a Mini Cooper struck them from behind. Sajeev's Instagram video showed reckless driving, with a speedometer reaching 220kmph prior to the incident. Police suspect he was intoxicated during the accident, with ongoing investigations. Further inquiries into alcohol service by local bars are also being conducted.
item.dc:creator: KANISHK SHARMA

item.title: SBI Research recommends LTCG on equities to be scrapped; calls for DTAA clarity
item.description: The proposal is aimed at making foreign capital flows into equities more stable and limiting the chances of abrupt withdrawals that could put pressure on the rupee. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) currently face a 12.5% LTCG tax on equity investments. The Union Budget 2026 retained this rate for listed shares and equity mutual funds, continuing the tax framework introduced as part of a major fiscal overhaul in 2024.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: Bank cut Rs 5.89 crore FD rate from 7.75% to 3.5%; Court orders higher interest
item.description: Initially, the FD earned interest at rates of 7.75%, 8.25% and 7.75% over different periods. However, from January 30, 2018, the bank lowered the rate to 3.5%. Challenging the reduction, the deposit holder approached the court again, arguing that the bank had cut the interest rate without any valid reason or justification.
